sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 1%, non-anginal chest pain to about 2% and atypical angina to about 12%; through this sum alone, being a woman lowers it to about 1% (being a woman also acts through the flat ST segment booster, below); a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 26% at 118 to about 21% at 175 beats per minute, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 19%.

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 23% at 0 to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; a reversible defect on the thallium scan raises it to about 47%; and more ST depression on exercise (from about 16% at 0 mm to about 50% at 2.8 mm), higher cholesterol (from about 13% at 193 mg/dL to about 45% at 308 mg/dL) and older age (from about 17% at 42 to about 28% at 66 years) raise it steadily.

Through this sum alone, a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 75% and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG to about 32%; both also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Two less common results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 15 and 17): a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the risk to about 8%, and through this sum alone a downsloping ST segment raises it to about 27%; the model ignores resting blood pressure.

This part combines the slope of the ST segment with a smaller part that reads sex, the resting ECG and chest pain on exercise, not as a simple sum, and acts on 111 of 242 training patients, nearly all with a flat ST segment, 72 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 96% without it and about 97% with it.
Through it, a flat ST segment raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 29%.

The smaller part inside it switches on only for women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, and raises the predicted risk of the typical such patient from about 12% to about 92% (the model has little data on this, n = 8).

Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the predicted risk more when the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy: it falls from about 33% to about 1% with those signs, against about 23% to about 1% without them.
This part relays the resting ECG and barely changes the predictions: through it, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy raise a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 24%.

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: additive composition. The logit z of node 0 is a linear score over 17 direct standardized inputs (dominated by ca 1.93, sex:1 1.67, cp:4 1.21, slope:2 1.05, chol 0.72, oldpeak 0.71) plus 0.772 x flat_slope_amplifier plus 0.026 x restecg2_relay; 7 inputs (trestbps, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:1, thal:3, thal:4) are disconnected. get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU, but for this binary task the model output is sigmoid(z) on the pre-activation (compute_performance train AUC 0.945 equals AUC of z; sigmoid(relu(z)) would give 0.912). Evidence (train, n=242, local forward passes): direct-linear logit SD 4.33 vs amplifier term SD 0.79 vs relay term SD 0.026. Dropping the amplifier term lowers train AUC 0.945 -> 0.930 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.868; the direct linear part alone gives AUC 0.931. So the network is essentially logistic regression plus one sparse nonlinear correction: a flat-slope bonus (+0.34 logit) and a large boost (+4.7 logit) for the 7 women with exertional angina, no LVH and flat ST slope. Kernel SHAP on the full model (train) ranks ca 0.149, sex:1 0.130, slope:2 0.121, cp:4 0.116, oldpeak 0.049, thal:7 0.046, chol 0.044 (mean |SHAP| on probability). Function preservation after the two input splits: max abs err 1.8e-15.

parts.name: flat_slope_amplifier
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: serial composition H(G(sex:0, exang:0, restecg:2), slope:2). Node 3598 = relu(1.51 slope:2 + 1.05 G - 0.76) and node 1650 = relu(1.29 G + 1.31*3598 - 0.73). Because G takes only the values 0 or 2.117 and slope:2 is binary, 1650 has exactly four regimes on train: G=0 & slope not flat -> 0 (n=131, 27% positive); G=0 & flat slope (slope:2) -> 0.446 (n=103, 63% positive); G on & slope not flat -> 2.097 (n=1, negative); G on & flat slope -> 6.092 (n=7, all positive). parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 665 is a three-way AND gate that fires only for women (sex:0 set) with exercise-induced angina (exang:0 unset, i.e. exang=yes) and no left-ventricular hypertrophy on resting ECG (restecg:2 unset). The restecg:2 chain 2349 -> 2771 never leaves the ReLU linear region on standardized one-hot inputs (2349 in [1.15,3.11], 2771 in [1.99,3.72]), so the gate collapses exactly to relu(1.41 sex:0 - 1.71 exang:0 - 1.18 restecg:2 - 3.39). Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation max is 2.117, reached only when all three conditions hold; removing any one condition drives it negative (no female: -0.86; no exang: -2.53; LVH present: -0.24). The gate is active on 8/242 rows (3.3%), always at the single value 2.117, and 7 of those 8 are positive cases. confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

ann_28.text: This part acts on 8 of 242 training patients (3%); nearly all of them are women and patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise.

For a typical patient it acts on, it raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 12% without this part to about 92% with it (on the training data only). The model has little data on this: only 8 training patients (patients the part acts on).
In the training data, 7 of these 8 patients had heart disease.

The model gives a clearly lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient is a woman than if the patient is a man, and even more so if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy: for a typical patient, going from male to female moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 33% to about 1% if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, and from about 23% to about 1% if resting ECG is something other than signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG.

Other effects: chest pain brought on by exercise (rather than no chest pain on exercise) raises it; signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than any other resting ECG) lowers it; female (rather than male) raises it (on the training data only).
Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: sex depending on exercise-induced angina lowers it; exercise-induced angina depending on resting ECG raises it.

ann_29.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a slightly higher predicted risk of heart disease if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy (about 24%) than if resting ECG is something other than signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (about 23%) (on the training data only).
This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.7 percentage points).

ann_30.text: This part acts on 111 of 242 training patients (46%); nearly all of them are patients with a flat ST segment.
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 96% without this part to about 97% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 72 of these 111 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 29%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 23%) (on the training data only).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: chest pain brought on by exercise (rather than no chest pain on exercise) raises it; signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than any other resting ECG) lowers it; female (rather than male) raises it; slope of the ST segment at peak exercise depending on exercise-induced angina raises it (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 23% at 0 vessels to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 80%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 23%) (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 75%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 23%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 16% at 0.0 mm to about 50% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 13% at 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to about 45% at 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) (on the training data only).

Other effects: a reversible defect on the thallium scan (rather than any other thallium stress test result) raises it; female (rather than male) lowers it; female (rather than male) lowers it; typical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; non-anginal chest pain (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; a fixed defect on the thallium scan (rather than any other thallium stress test result) lowers it; a higher age raises it steadily; atypical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; and 2 still smaller effects listed in the evidence table (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily; a downsloping ST segment (rather than an upsloping ST segment) raises it; a downsloping ST segment (rather than an upsloping ST segment) raises it; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (rather than fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less) lowers it; chest pain brought on by exercise (rather than no chest pain on exercise) raises it (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 17 training patients (a downsloping ST segment).

summary.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 23% at 0 vessels to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

The model gives a clearly lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient is a woman than if the patient is a man, and even more so if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy: for a typical patient, going from male to female moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 33% to about 1% if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, and from about 23% to about 1% if resting ECG is something other than signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG.

The model gives a slightly higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment, and even more so if exercise brings on chest pain: for a typical patient, going from slope of the ST segment at peak exercise other than a flat ST segment to a flat ST segment moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 23% to about 80% if exercise brings on chest pain, and from about 23% to about 80% if exercise does not bring on chest pain (on the training data only).
